questions.scenario: A landlord is listed as the certificate holder on a certificate of insurance that a tenant's agent issued showing the tenant's liability policy. The policy itself contains no endorsement naming the landlord. The landlord is later sued over an injury in the tenant's space.
questions.stem: What rights does the certificate give the landlord under the tenant's policy?

choices.text: None beyond what the policy itself expressly provides
choices.rationale: Correct: § 502(c) says a certificate does not confer any rights beyond those expressly provided by the referenced policy.

choices.text: The same rights as an additional insured on the policy
choices.rationale: Incorrect: additional-insured status must come from the policy (an endorsement), not from the certificate.

choices.text: The right to defense but not to indemnity
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the certificate creates no defense rights that the policy doesn't already provide.

choices.text: The rights of a named insured, since the holder is named
choices.rationale: Incorrect: a certificate holder is, by definition, a person other than the policyholder.

questions.explanation: Ins. Law § 501(b) defines a certificate holder as a person, other than a policyholder, identified on the certificate. § 502(c): a certificate shall not amend, extend or alter the coverage and shall not confer any rights beyond those expressly provided by the policy. To be protected, the landlord would need to be added to the policy itself (for example, by an additional insured endorsement).
questions.memoryTip: A certificate is a snapshot of the policy, not a key to it.

keyPoints.label: Certificate is only evidence of coverage
Confers no rights beyond the policy

questions.scenario: A property owner tells a contractor it will not release payment for finished work unless the contractor's liability certificate is issued on the owner's own custom form, which neither the insurer nor the superintendent has approved.
questions.stem: Under NY Insurance Law § 502, is the owner's demand permitted?

choices.text: Yes, because payment terms are purely a private contract matter
choices.rationale: Incorrect: § 502(a) specifically restricts conditioning payment on a certificate in a non-approved form.

choices.text: Yes, if the contractor's agent agrees to sign it
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the producer's willingness does not make an unapproved form acceptable.

choices.text: No; it must accept an insurer form or an approved standard form
choices.rationale: Correct: a certificate may be required only on the insurer's form or a standard/other form approved by the superintendent.

choices.text: No; owners may never require certificates of insurance
choices.rationale: Incorrect: requiring a certificate is allowed; only the form (and added terms) is restricted.

questions.explanation: § 502(a): no person or governmental entity shall wilfully require, as a condition of awarding a contract, of work proceeding, or of payment, the issuance of a liability certificate unless it is (1) a form promulgated by the insurer issuing the policy or (2) a standard certificate form from an industry standard-setting organization approved by the superintendent, or another superintendent-approved form.
questions.memoryTip: Certificates come on approved forms — not homemade ones.

keyPoints.label: Custom unapproved form cannot be required
Insurer form or superintendent-approved standard form

questions.stem: Which action does NY Insurance Law § 502 expressly allow a project owner to take regarding a bidder's insurance?

choices.text: Require the certificate to guarantee coverage the policy lacks
choices.rationale: Incorrect: § 502(b) bars requiring certificate terms or guarantees that the policy does not expressly include.

choices.text: State minimum insurance limits in its bid solicitation
choices.rationale: Correct: § 502(b) does not prohibit minimum insurance requirements or coverage limits in a competitive bid solicitation.

choices.text: Rewrite the certificate to extend the policy period
choices.rationale: Incorrect: a certificate cannot amend, extend or alter coverage (§ 502(c)).

choices.text: Insist the certificate add the owner as a named insured
choices.rationale: Incorrect: a certificate cannot change who is insured under the policy.

questions.explanation: § 502(b) prohibits wilfully requiring certificate language, warranties or guarantees that the referenced policy does not expressly include, but it does not stop anyone from including minimum insurance requirements, limits or other conditions in a bid solicitation, or from requesting clarification of policy terms from the insurer or producer.
questions.memoryTip: Ask for limits in the bid; don't make the certificate lie.

questions.stem: Who may penalize a person who wilfully violates New York's certificate of insurance law?

choices.text: The certificate holder, through a private fine
choices.rationale: Incorrect: Article 5 gives the penalty power to the superintendent, not to private parties.

choices.text: The insurer that issued the referenced policy
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the insurer has no statutory power to fine violators.

choices.text: The Excess Line Association of New York
choices.rationale: Incorrect: ELANY stamps excess line documents; it does not enforce Article 5.

choices.text: The superintendent, after notice and a hearing
choices.rationale: Correct: § 503 lets the superintendent, after notice and hearing, order a wilful violator (other than a governmental entity) to pay a penalty.

questions.explanation: Ins. Law § 503: if the superintendent finds, after notice and hearing, that a person other than a governmental entity wilfully violated Article 5, the superintendent may order a monetary penalty, larger for repeat violations. § 504 lets the superintendent adopt rules to carry out the article.

questions.scenario: Rosa's new homeowners policy has been in force for 30 days when the insurer decides to cancel it.
questions.stem: Under NY Insurance Law § 3425, what must the cancellation notice include?

choices.text: The specific reason or reasons for the cancellation
choices.rationale: Correct: § 3425(b) requires notices issued in the first 60 days to state or be accompanied by the specific reason(s).

choices.text: Nothing special, since any notice is valid in 60 days
choices.rationale: Incorrect: even during the first 60 days the specific reason must be given.

choices.text: Proof that the superintendent approved the cancellation
choices.rationale: Incorrect: no prior superintendent approval is required.

choices.text: An offer to rewrite the policy through the FAIR Plan
choices.rationale: Incorrect: § 3425 does not require the insurer to offer FAIR Plan coverage.

questions.explanation: § 3425(b): during the first 60 days a covered policy is in effect, no notice of cancellation shall be issued or effective unless it states or is accompanied by the specific reason or reasons. After 60 days (or on a renewal), cancellation is limited to the grounds listed in § 3425(c).
questions.memoryTip: First 60 days: you can cancel, but you must say why.

questions.stem: When an insurer mails a § 3425 cancellation notice to a named insured, when must a copy go to the insured's agent or broker?

choices.text: Only if the insured requests it in writing
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the copy is required, not optional.

choices.text: Within seven days of mailing it to the insured
choices.rationale: Correct: § 3425(h)(3) requires the copy within seven days of the mailing to the named insured.

choices.text: At least 45 days before the policy period ends
choices.rationale: Incorrect: 45–60 days is the window for nonrenewal notices to the insured, not the agent's copy.

choices.text: Within 30 days after the cancellation is effective
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the copy is due within seven days of the insured's notice being mailed.

questions.explanation: § 3425(h)(3): a copy of every cancellation or nonrenewal notice shall be mailed, delivered or transmitted to the insured's authorized agent or broker within seven days of the time the notice is mailed to the named insured.
questions.memoryTip: Insured gets the notice; the agent gets a copy within a week.

questions.stem: Under NY Insurance Law § 3425, an insurer may NOT refuse to issue or renew a covered personal lines or auto policy solely because of the applicant's:

choices.text: Fraud in presenting a prior claim
choices.rationale: Incorrect choice: fraud or material misrepresentation is a recognized ground for cancellation.

choices.text: Failure to pay the premium billed
choices.rationale: Incorrect choice: nonpayment of premium is a permitted ground.

choices.text: Advanced age
choices.rationale: Correct: § 3425(i) bars refusing to issue or renew a covered policy solely on the ground of advanced age.

choices.text: Reckless acts increasing the hazard
choices.rationale: Incorrect choice: willful or reckless acts increasing the hazard are a permitted ground for personal lines.

questions.explanation: § 3425(i): no insurer shall refuse to issue or renew a covered policy solely on the ground of the advanced age of the applicant or insured. Nonpayment, fraud or material misrepresentation, and willful or reckless acts increasing the hazard are listed grounds in § 3425(c).
questions.memoryTip: Age alone is never the reason.

questions.scenario: Jamal's personal auto policy has been in force for five months. His teenage son, who customarily drives one of the insured cars, has his driver's license suspended. Jamal has paid all premiums and made no misrepresentations.
questions.stem: May the insurer cancel the auto policy mid-term?

choices.text: No, because the son is not the named insured
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the ground covers any person who customarily operates an insured auto, not only the named insured.

choices.text: No, auto policies cannot be cancelled after 60 days
choices.rationale: Incorrect: they can, but only for the grounds listed in § 3425(c)(1).

choices.text: Yes, for any reason stated in the notice
choices.rationale: Incorrect: after 60 days, the reason must be one of the statutory grounds.

choices.text: Yes, since a customary driver's license was suspended
choices.rationale: Correct: § 3425(c)(1)(B) permits cancellation for suspension or revocation of the license of a customary operator.

questions.explanation: After an auto policy has been in effect 60 days, § 3425(c)(1) allows cancellation only for (A) nonpayment of premium, (B) suspension or revocation during the required policy period of the driver's license of the named insured or any other person who customarily operates an insured automobile, or (C) fraud or material misrepresentation in obtaining the policy or presenting a claim.
questions.memoryTip: Auto after 60 days: Pay, License, Lies.

keyPoints.label: License suspension of customary driver is a ground

questions.scenario: Helen's homeowners policy was first issued 18 months ago. She has paid every premium, made no misrepresentations, and her home has not changed. The insurer wants to nonrenew at the next anniversary because it is reducing its homeowners writings in her region.
questions.stem: Under NY Insurance Law § 3425, may the insurer nonrenew at that anniversary?

choices.text: Yes, with notice 45 to 60 days before the anniversary
choices.rationale: Incorrect: proper notice is not enough during the required policy period; a cancellation ground is also needed.

choices.text: No; during the three-year period it needs a cancellation ground
choices.rationale: Correct: § 3425(e) bars nonrenewal effective during the required policy period unless a ground for cancellation exists.

choices.text: Yes, because a homeowners policy runs for one year at a time
choices.rationale: Incorrect: for personal lines the required policy period is three years.

choices.text: No, homeowners policies can never be nonrenewed in New York
choices.rationale: Incorrect: nonrenewal is allowed with proper notice once the required policy period ends.

questions.explanation: For personal lines, § 3425(a)(7) sets a three-year required policy period from first issuance or voluntary renewal, and § 3425(e) says no notice of nonrenewal or conditional renewal may take effect during that period unless it is based on a ground for which the policy could have been cancelled. Reducing business in a region is not such a ground, so the insurer must wait until the period ends (and then give 45–60 days' notice).
questions.memoryTip: Homeowners: three-year promise unless there's a cancellation reason.

keyPoints.label: Nonrenewal only on a cancellation ground during the period

questions.stem: How does NY Insurance Law § 3425 treat a personal umbrella liability policy for cancellation and nonrenewal purposes?

choices.text: As a covered personal lines policy under § 3425
choices.rationale: Correct: § 3425(a)(3) states a personal umbrella liability policy is a 'covered policy' under the personal lines definition.

choices.text: As commercial excess coverage governed by § 3426
choices.rationale: Incorrect: a personal umbrella is expressly placed within § 3425's personal lines definition.

choices.text: As exempt, since it only sits above other policies
choices.rationale: Incorrect: being excess over underlying policies does not remove it from § 3425.

choices.text: As an auto policy with a one-year required period
choices.rationale: Incorrect: it is treated as personal lines insurance, not automobile insurance.

questions.explanation: § 3425(a)(3): a personal umbrella liability policy shall be considered a covered policy under the personal lines definition in paragraph (a)(2). It therefore receives personal lines cancellation, nonrenewal and required-policy-period protections, rather than the commercial rules of § 3426.

questions.stem: Which reason for declining a New York fire insurance application is consistent with NY Insurance Law § 3429?

choices.text: The home is in a county the insurer has chosen to avoid
choices.rationale: Incorrect: refusing based solely on geographic location within the state is prohibited.

choices.text: The applicant's ZIP code has many low-income residents
choices.rationale: Incorrect: this is geographic redlining, not risk-based underwriting.

choices.text: The insurer has too few agents near the applicant's town
choices.rationale: Incorrect: this is still a decision based on location rather than on the risk.

choices.text: Sound underwriting criteria tied to expected loss experience
choices.rationale: Correct: § 3429 allows refusals based on sound underwriting and actuarial principles reasonably related to actual or anticipated loss experience.

questions.explanation: § 3429(a) prohibits refusing to issue or renew, or cancelling, fire (or fire and extended coverage) and § 3425 auto policies based solely on the geographical location of the risk within New York. It does not preclude decisions based on sound underwriting and actuarial principles reasonably related to actual or anticipated loss experience.
questions.memoryTip: Underwrite the RISK, not the MAP.

questions.scenario: After being turned down by every insurer she contacted, Denise files a complaint with the superintendent claiming she was denied homeowners insurance because of where her house is located. The insurers say her house has serious physical defects.
questions.stem: What may the superintendent do in investigating the complaint under § 3430?

choices.text: Order an insurer to issue a policy before investigating
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the statute provides investigation tools; it does not require issuing coverage before the facts are determined.

choices.text: Refer the complaint to the FAIR Plan for decision
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the superintendent investigates the complaint; the FAIR Plan does not decide it.

choices.text: Require a property inspection, hold a hearing, or both
choices.rationale: Correct: § 3430(b) lets the superintendent require physical inspection of the risk or hold a hearing, or both.

choices.text: Dismiss it, since insurers may consider any physical defect
choices.rationale: Incorrect: the superintendent must investigate whether the denial was based on location rather than sound underwriting.

questions.explanation: § 3430(a) lets an insured who cannot obtain homeowners or fire insurance (other than from the NY Property Insurance Underwriting Association), or auto insurance (other than through the NY Automobile Insurance Plan), because of geographic location file a complaint. Under § 3430(b), the superintendent investigates and may require a physical inspection of the property or hold a hearing, or both, to resolve whether the denial reflected location or sound underwriting.
questions.memoryTip: Location complaint → inspect the house, hear the case.
